F7.label: Insider purchase cluster
F7.citation: Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (2012), Journal of Finance 67(3)
F7.effect: In US insider trades from 1986 to 2007, a long-short portfolio of opportunistic (non-routine) insider buys minus opportunistic sells earned value-weighted abnormal returns of about 82 basis points a month, while routine insiders' trades earned about zero.

ownEstimate.note: Conservative column: return minus beta x SPY (no market-model alpha, which inflates post-decline buys), t two-way clustered by issuer and month, p one-sided. Market-model CAR: 1.56% (t 4.67 by date). Matched-control outcome also positive. About 40% of events are at since-delisted issuers missing from the price source (survivorship, direction unknown). Before costs. Full tables: docs/f7-study.md.

F6.label: Late filing notice (NT 10-K / NT 10-Q)
F6.effect: Among 2,115 first-time late filers (fiscal periods 2000-2008), the mean abnormal return over the five days around the NT filing was about -2.93% for NT 10-Q and -1.96% for NT 10-K filings (figures to verify against the published tables before display).

F5.label: Customer bankruptcy
F5.citation: Jorion & Zhang (2009), Journal of Finance 64(5); Hertzel, Li, Officer & Rodgers (2008), Journal of Financial Economics 87(2)
F5.effect: Around 251 Chapter 11 filings from 1999 to 2005, industrial creditors of the bankrupt firm had an average abnormal return of about -2.29% over the 11 days around the filing (financial creditors about -0.34%); Hertzel et al. report negative, significant stock price effects for suppliers of firms filing for bankruptcy.

F1.label: Customer guidance or news (supplier read-through)
F1.effect: Supplier stock returns follow their principal customers' past returns with a lag; a long-short strategy on this customer momentum earned monthly alphas of over 150 basis points in the original sample (about 1981-2004, period to verify in the paper).

F8.label: Activist 13D stake
F8.citation: Brav, Jiang, Partnoy & Thomas (2008), Journal of Finance 63(4)
F8.effect: In hand-collected US hedge fund activism events from 2001 to 2006, targets earned an abnormal return of about 7% around the announcement, with no reversal over the following year.
